claim_classifications.phase17_claim: Mean MFE equals Mean MAE exactly, proving symmetric Brownian motion.
claim_classifications.audit_evidence: Pooled MFE and MAE were mathematically identical because pooled_mfe = 0.5*(MFE_L + MFE_S) and pooled_mae = 0.5*(MAE_L + MAE_S) are identical by definition (Short MFE == Long MAE). Additionally, Phase 17's forward slice had an off-by-one error (overstated MFE by ~$0.04/oz).

The equality was an algebraic artifact of the pooling definition.

p17_nan_sorting_bug_audit.root_cause: Column 'is_daily_roll_window' had variance=0, producing 0/0 = NaN in np.corrcoef. np.argsort followed by array reversal [::-1] placed NaNs at the top of the array, causing Phase 17 to display NaN pairs instead of the true perfect linear duplicates.

passive_exposure_claim_audit.claim: Candidate 5 2024 gain was entirely attributable to passive long exposure
passive_exposure_claim_audit.factual_reconciliation: In Fold 3 (2024), Long trades generated +$71.07 on 30 trades while Short trades lost -$13.50 on 151 trades, netting +$57.57. Thus, Long trades indeed accounted for >100% of the net profit. However, the claim that the model had 'passive long exposure' requires caveat: Candidate 5 was actually heavily net short in execution volume (151 short signals vs 30 long signals). The profit was generated because the few long signals occurred during explosive upward legs, while the 151 short trades had small per-trade drag (-$0.089/trade) that was masked by the longs.

verdict_rationale: Phase 17's core empirical diagnosis (cost friction dominance, negative net expectancy, model failure vs baselines, and the necessity to STOP the current M5 approach) is completely verified and confirmed. However, Phase 17 contained four specific technical/methodological flaws: (1) Claiming MFE=MAE proves Brownian motion when it was an algebraic identity of the pooling formula; (2) An off-by-one index slice in excursion calculations (1-bar lookahead into exit candle); (3) Using an uncorrected N/H heuristic for Neff which overstated degrees-of-freedom reduction by ~40%; and (4) A NaN-sorting bug in top collinear feature pairs caused by zero-variance column 'is_daily_roll_window'. All four errors are fully corrected in this Phase 18A forensic audit. The corrected evidence continues to conclusively support stopping the current M5 intraday approach. A macro-horizon research redesign may be proposed under strict pre-specified conditions.
